    <h1>Corey S. Sparks, Ph.D.</h1>
    <p class="lead-role">Professor, Department of Sociology and Demography &middot; The University of Texas at San Antonio</p>
    <p>
      I am a demographer and quantitative social scientist whose work sits at the
      intersection of population health, spatial analysis, and applied statistics.
      My research examines how demographic and contextual conditions shape human
      health, with particular attention to mortality, maternal and child health,
      food insecurity, and the geographic inequalities that structure these outcomes.
    </p>
    <p>
      Methodologically, I work with large survey and administrative datasets and
      apply hierarchical, spatial, and Bayesian models, machine learning, and
      reproducible analytic workflows in R. I have published more than forty
      peer-reviewed articles across population health, spatial demography, and
      quantitative methods, and I teach graduate courses in statistical and spatial
      analysis for population science.
    </p>

## Book

::: {.book-feature}
### Applied Demographic Data Analysis

A hands-on guide to statistical methods for demographers, covering survey data
analysis, macrodemographic analysis, and microdemographic event history models,
with an emphasis on practical application in R rather than theoretical proofs.

[Read the book &rarr;](https://coreysparks.github.io/appdem_Book/){.book-link}
:::

## Research areas

::: {.research-area}
### Spatial demography and geographic inequality

I study how health, mortality, and social outcomes vary across place, using
geospatial methods and spatial statistical models to analyze segregation, poverty,
residential structure, and local clustering. This work emphasizes results that
clarify where disparities concentrate and why.
:::

::: {.research-area}
### Population health and mortality

Much of my research examines mortality, maternal health, substance use, and
nutrition using large administrative and public health datasets, with a focus on
which populations are most affected and how contextual conditions shape risk.
:::

::: {.research-area}
### Statistical and predictive methods

I develop and apply hierarchical models, Bayesian estimation, forecasting, and
machine learning to demographic problems, favoring methods that are transparent,
reproducible, and interpretable.
:::

::: {.research-area}
### Workforce and life-course demography

I also study longer-term trajectories, including labor market entry, cohort
transitions, and social mobility, using longitudinal and cohort-based analytics
to identify structural drivers and key inflection points.
:::
